queryPlanning.finding: Exact query-set agreement was zero for both models on both hard tasks. Mean lexical query-set Jaccard ranged from 0 to 0.1333, although the plans were often semantically similar.
queryPlanning.importantFailure: Both models initially focused the stock task on identifying the +755% company and usually omitted downstream target-price, parent-company, and dated-close queries that depend on the discovered identity.

providers.openai: Relevant but unstable on four of eight fixed queries; worst top-1 agreement 0 and set Jaccard 0.0476.
providers.naver: Three Korean person queries were perfectly stable while available, but burst repetition triggered failures and later finance queries were unavailable.
providers.duckduckgo: Partially relevant, then repeated-query failures made the finance probes unavailable.
providers.bing: Available and fast, but several stable Korean results were irrelevant; stability alone was not quality.

laterCandidates.reason: Pairwise consensus improved fixed-query set overlap offline, but live Terra repeats produced current-public-fact accuracy 0/2 then 2/2; the person choice remained unstable.
Stage classification became stable after clarification, but two live Terra repeats both scored current-public-fact 0/2 and one closed-set positive control regressed.
Terra kept the current facts in both repeats after adjudication correction and reduced cost, but gpt-5.5 exceeded the 300-second boundary on its first task.

The full source Receipt and instruction-authority boundary were preserved, but the added extraction model made the first hard task take about three minutes and the repeat about two and a half minutes. The owner defined both durations as categorically unacceptable for web search, so the run was terminated before gpt-5.5 qualification.
laterCandidates.rawEvidence: not promoted because the qualification was intentionally terminated at the user-time stop line

ownerTimeBoundary.statement: 300 seconds and 2.5 minutes are both categorically unacceptable for what a human experiences as web search.

modes.waiting: The user remains in front of the conversation for a request such as search this. This requires an absolute human latency ceiling in the tens-of-seconds class.
modes.delegated: The user explicitly hands off a long investigation or deliverable and leaves. This is governed by visible progress, intermediate verification, stop, resume, and honest completion rather than the same short ceiling.

ownerTimeBoundary.effect: Accuracy or token reduction cannot qualify this waiting-mode W9 candidate after it crosses the human waiting boundary. The candidate loop stops instead of opening another architecture in the same Gate.

futureStructuralConvergence.observation: After serial search, provider selection, staged search, projection, and serial extraction all failed a conjunction of truth and human time, branch-parallel isolated investigation remains a plausible way to reduce waiting wall time.
futureStructuralConvergence.boundary: This is recorded only as future evidence for the already-separate delegation and time-axis track. W9 does not open multi-agent implementation or treat parallelism as qualified.

next.gate: W9 remains incomplete; the current patch family reached its stop line with no qualified product change.
next.work: Before any new W9 implementation, seal a waiting-mode everyday-web latency budget and representative field sample. Keep delegated long-form research under its separate progress, intermediate verification, stop, and resume contract.
nonGoals: more K-BrowseComp tuning in this patch family
